source.title: Mitigating Communication Costs in Neural Networks: The Role of Dendritic Nonlinearity
source.authors: Xundong Wu; Pengfei Zhao; Zilin Yu; Lei Ma; Ka-Wa Yip; Hua-Jin Tang; Gang Pan; Tie-Jun Huang

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports dendritic-architecture performance comparisons, but does not test double descent or use the double-descent finding. It does not vary training epochs or sample size to test the claimed curves, and its architecture comparisons do not establish a peak near interpolation.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on test performance when changing dendritic architecture, width, and computational or communication budgets. These are adjacent to model-capacity questions but do not test any listed double-descent version. It does not report a sweep over model size through an interpolation threshold, an epoch-wise curve, or a sample-size sweep. The authors' discussions of dendritic learning capacity are not results about double descent.
record.test_reason: The paper compares dendritic and point-neuron networks at matched computational or communication budgets on ImageNet, CIFAR-100 and LibriSpeech. It never sweeps model size through an interpolation threshold, never tracks test error over epochs, never varies sample size, and never mentions double descent. It neither tests nor uses the finding. The record's 'discusses' overstates the relation, since the text has no discussion of double descent at all.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: the authors conclude dendritic nonlinearities do not substantially affect learning capacity. Their main benefit is expanding capacity while cutting communication and memory-access costs through local feature aggregation.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares dendritic and point-neuron architectures for performance and communication cost; it does not implement a double-descent experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported performance depends on architecture, dendrite count, width, sparsity, dataset, and computational or communication budget.

fits_no_version.finding: At matched compute, dendritic ResNet-18-style models match point-neuron models when Ψ ≥ 0.25, in both dense and 85%-sparse settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dendritic aggregation can reduce inter-layer neuron count without loss of accuracy at fixed parameter count.

fits_no_version.finding: Replacing a compact transformer's feedforward bottleneck with a dendritic layer lowers ImageNet accuracy from 80.9% to 80.6%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A dendritic replacement for the transformer feedforward block costs little accuracy while cutting peak activation I/O.

fits_no_version.finding: On LibriSpeech at fixed communication cost, test error falls from 15.39 (K=1) to 10.49 (K=4) to 8.23 (K=16). At matched compute, dendritic models are comparable or slightly worse.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At a fixed communication budget, more dendrites per neuron improve speech-recognition error.

record.code_released: The paper says the code will be openly accessible upon publication; no URL is stated.
record.problems: The paper does not test any double-descent version. Several image-classification results are described qualitatively or shown in plots rather than stated numerically; the LibriSpeech tables give test errors without uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: Not applicable; no rows were omitted for the row limit.

untested.parts: No model-size sweep through the interpolation threshold. Width scaling uses only a few levels, all far from interpolation, with no peak reported.
No capacity sweep past interpolation in any model class.
No effective-complexity measure predicting a peak location.
No label-noise or regularization manipulation related to a peak.
No re-counting of complexity via effective parameters.

record.verdict_notes: Irrelevant to double descent. The study was likely retrieved on 'capacity' keywords. Relation changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only'; 'uses_without_test' would also fit T6, but neither use nor discussion occurs in the text.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size sweep through the interpolation threshold or fall-rise-fall test-error curve.
No test-error measurements over training epochs.
No comparison varying the number of training samples near an interpolation threshold.
No double-descent tests across model classes or capacity sweeps past interpolation.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as a predictor of peak location.
No tests of noise, multiple peaks, or optimally tuned regularization in relation to a double-descent peak.
No re-counting of complexity by effective parameters or test of whether that produces an ordinary U-shaped curve.
